questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

text:
Hello,

I work part-time in the office of Steinbruch Trading Ltd in Kreuzlingen and I'm writing because I honestly don't know where I stand any more.

On 12 March 2026 my manager, Isla Schmid, called me into her room and told me the company was 'reorganising' the admin side. She said my hours would probably go down and that I should 'think about my future'. I earn CHF 2,120 a month as it is, and if my hours are cut I'd be losing around CHF 420 a month, which I really can't manage with my rent.

Since that talk a colleague, Ben Weber, told me that Ms Schmid said in a team meeting that I 'won't be around much longer'. When I asked her about it she just smiled and said we would talk another time.

I want to be clear about one thing: nobody has given me notice. There has been no letter, and Ms Schmid has never said to my face that I'm being let go either. It's all hints and rumours.

I've been with the company since August 2022 and my reviews have always been good. It feels like they are trying to push me into leaving by myself so they don't have to do anything. Is that allowed? Can they just cut my hours because they feel like it? I'd like to know what I can do and whether it makes sense to talk to someone from your side.

Thank you for reading this.

Alice Widmer
Wiesenstrasse 2, Kreuzlingen
